prerequisites: knowledge in mechanics and elasticity theory

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire insight into design according to the limit state method, using partial safety factors.
Acquire insight into the structural behavior of steel and wood structural components.
Develop more general skills: working in a group, written reporting.

Based on a concrete structure, students learn to develop a design in both wood and steel. The background and specificity of each material and the resulting structural material behavior are examined in detail. The emphasis is on how this structural behavior is translated into design rules as used in design standards.
Emphasis is also placed on the practical application of current design codes (EC0, EC 1, EC3 and EC5).
The design addresses various structural components, such as beams and columns, as well as detailing including welds and bolted connections.
Second-order effects (buckling and lateral-torsional buckling) are included due to the slenderness of the structural components.
More general skills such as group work and written reporting are developed.

syllabus_topics: Design of structural components in wood or steel according to the limit state method
EN 1990 Basis of structural design: safety, loads, load effects, material properties, and resistance
Loads acting on structures according to Eurocode 1: self-weights and imposed loads, snow load, and wind load on buildings
Eurocode 3 for the calculation of steel structures (EN 1993, Part 1-1: General rules and rules for buildings)
Lateral-torsional buckling of flexurally loaded beams
EN 1993-1-8 related to connections: bolted connections, welds, and column bases
Eurocode 5 for the calculation of steel structures (EN 1995, Part 1-1: General rules and rules for buildings)
Material properties of wood: fiber orientation, equilibrium moisture content, load duration, and creep behavior
EN 1991-2-1: Actions on Structures – Densities, self-weight and imposed loads
EN 1991-2-3: Actions on structures – snow loads
EN 1991-2-4: Actions on structures – wind loads
assessment_rules: Evaluation is continuous without an exam during the examination period. Assessment methods include a design/product, a take-home assignment, and a report. Question formats are open questions. Learning materials allowed are course material, formula sheet, calculator, and computer.
